question.summary: The source asked whether polynomial entanglement invariants are complete, that is whether agreement of all polynomial invariants forces two states to be related by local unitaries. Sudbery answered affirmatively by applying the Onishchik-Vinberg theorem on orbits of compact linear groups.
question.importance: Completeness would reduce local-unitary classification of entanglement to evaluating polynomials, and the bipartite and multipartite cases are far more delicate than the unipartite case because the symmetry group is a product of local unitaries rather than the full unitary group.

targetClauses.label: Completeness of polynomial entanglement invariants
targetClauses.text: The archived statement asks whether the polynomial entanglement invariants of bipartite and multipartite density operators are complete, that is whether equality of all polynomial invariants on two states implies they are related by local unitaries.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: A proof that the polynomial invariants separate local-unitary orbits, or two states with identical invariants that are not locally unitarily equivalent.

claims.title: Compact-group invariants separate local unitary orbits
claims.text: Sudbery answers the completeness question affirmatively by invoking the Onishchik-Vinberg theorem that the orbits of a compact linear group acting on a real vector space are separated by the polynomial invariants. The local unitary group is compact and acts linearly on the real space of density operators, so two multipartite states agree on all polynomial invariants exactly when they are related by a local unitary.

decisions.rationale: The archived completeness question follows directly from the cited compact-group separation theorem, and the source collection itself records Sudbery's solution in its Solution section.

cautions.label: Scope
cautions.text: Only the principal completeness question is settled; the accompanying sub-problems on finite complete generating sets in all dimensions, on higher-party multipartite classification, and on polynomial separability criteria remain active.

cautions.label: Scope
cautions.text: Compactness of the group is essential; the analogous separation statement is false for GL(n,C) similarity actions, as the Jordan-form obstruction shows.
